newsitem.title: CANADA: 150 Quebec youths arrested in national holiday riot.
newsitem.headline: 150 Quebec youths arrested in national holiday riot.

text.p: Police arrested 150 people early on Tuesday in Quebec's two main cities when youths rioted on the French-speaking province's nationalist holiday.
Some 100 youths were arrested in Quebec City, the provincial capital, and 48 were arrested in Montreal, the largest city.
A policeman was hurt in Quebec City when police clashed with hundreds of youths who broke shops windows. Three teenagers were also injured. Police said none of the injuries were severe.
In Montreal, youths went on a rampage, breaking shop windows near the city centre.
The violence erupted on the day of Quebec's patron saint, St. John the Baptist, a date Quebeckers celebrate as their "national" holiday.
"It was a riot. It felt like the youths were worked up. They were looking for a confrontation, but we limited the damage," a Quebec City spokesman said.

The trouble began after an outdoor concert attended by about 120,000 people on the Plains of Abraham, a park overlooking the St. Lawrence River where an English expeditionary force defeated French troops to conquer Quebec in 1759.

A crowd of several hundred youths tried to charge the provincial legislature, where rioters last year smashed windows in a similar rampage. The crowd then moved on to the city's old quarter and began throwing rocks and bottles at 500 police.
Riot police used tear gas to disperse the crowd. It took them about five hours to clear the streets of the 389-year-old city.
It was the sixth consecutive year that youths have rioted in Quebec City during the annual celebrations.
